overview.title: What is RIG
overview.tagline: Rust library for building portable, modular, and lightweight Fullstack AI Agents
overview.description: Rig is a Rust library for building LLM-powered applications that focuses on ergonomics and modularity. It provides full support for LLM completion and embedding workflows with simple but powerful abstractions.
key_features: Full support for LLM completion and embedding workflows
Simple but powerful common abstractions over LLM providers (OpenAI, Cohere, etc.) and vector stores (MongoDB, in-memory, etc.)
Integrate LLMs in your app with minimal boilerplate
Lightweight: Rust runs orders of magnitude faster than Python
Safety: Rust's type system and ownership model helps work with unexpected LLM outputs
Portability: Rust code can be compiled to WebAssembly (WASM support coming soon)

quick_start.title: Quick Start Guide
installation_steps: This adds rig-core dependency and Tokio (async Rust runtime)
Set up environment variable: OPENAI_API_KEY (for OpenAI examples)

basic_example.description: Simple example prompting OpenAI's GPT-4 model
basic_example.note: Using #[tokio::main] requires enabling tokio's macros and rt-multi-thread features: cargo add tokio --features macros,rt-multi-thread

completion_and_embedding_models.title: Completion and Embedding Models
completion_and_embedding_models.description: Rig provides a consistent API for working with LLMs and embeddings. Each provider (e.g. OpenAI, Cohere) has a Client struct that can be used to initialize completion and embedding models.
traits: CompletionModel: Common low-level interface for creating and executing completion requests
EmbeddingModel: Common low-level interface for creating and executing embedding requests
completion_and_embedding_models.features: Each model implements traits that provide consistent API across different providers

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: High-level abstractions over LLMs in the form of the Agent type
capabilities: Full-blown RAG systems for answering questions using a knowledge base
Context-aware agents that leverage connected information
agents.usage: The Agent type can be used to create anything from basic chatbots to sophisticated AI systems

vector_stores_and_indexes.title: Vector Stores and Indexes
vector_stores_and_indexes.description: Rig defines a common interface for working with vector stores and indexes

VectorStoreIndex: Interface for vector index implementations

modules.agent: Implementation of the Agent struct and its builder
modules.audio_generation: Everything related to audio generation (Text To Speech). Abstracts over different providers using the AudioGenerationModel trait
modules.client: Traits for defining and creating provider clients. Used to create models for completion, embeddings, etc.
modules.completion: Functionality for LLM completions and responses
modules.embeddings: Working with embeddings - numerical representations of documents. Used for NLP tasks like text classification, information retrieval, and document similarity
modules.extractor: High-level abstractions for extracting structured data from text using LLMs
modules.image_generation: Core image generation abstractions. Allows calling different providers using the ImageGenerationModel trait
modules.loaders: Utility structs for loading and preprocessing files
modules.pipeline: Flexible pipeline API for defining sequences of operations with or without AI components (semantic search, LLM prompting, etc.)
modules.providers: Clients for the different LLM providers that Rig supports
modules.streaming: Working with streaming completion models. Traits and types for streaming requests and responses
modules.telemetry: Orchestrate telemetry across pipelines and workflows. Includes tracing, OpenTelemetry collector support, and platform integrations like Langfuse
modules.tool: Tool-related structs and traits for agent capabilities
modules.transcription: Audio transcription models. Traits, structs, and enums for transcription requests and responses

architecture.title: Architecture and Design
rust_advantages: Lightweight: Runs orders of magnitude faster than Python, making running and deploying swarms of agents efficient
Safety: Type system and ownership model helps work with unexpected LLM outputs, coercing types and handling errors gracefully
Portability: Can be compiled to WebAssembly for running in web browsers (even local LLM models). Note: WASM support coming soon
design_principles: Ergonomics: Simple and intuitive API design
Modularity: Composable components that work together
Minimal boilerplate: Get started quickly with less code
Provider agnostic: Common abstractions across different providers
Type safety: Leverage Rust's type system for reliability
architecture.comparison: Rig provides similar functionality to Python/JS frameworks like Langchain, LlamaIndex, Marvin, and PyDantic, but with Rust's performance and safety advantages

contributing.description: Rig is an open-source project welcoming contributions from the community

model_provider_integrations.description: Add support for new language model providers
model_provider_integrations.location: Each provider integration is contained in its own module under rig-core/src/providers
model_provider_integrations.openai_compatible: If provider has OpenAI compatible API, document how to use existing openai integration instead of creating new module
model_provider_integrations.requirements: Should not require new dependencies not already in the project

vector_store_integrations.description: Add support for new vector stores
vector_store_integrations.location: Each integration is in its own crate in root directory with naming convention: rig-<store_name>
vector_store_integrations.reason: Separate crates because vector stores often require many additional dependencies
vector_store_integrations.testing: Consider adding integration tests (reference existing tests like Qdrant)
